researcher_notes: Sources swept: ExaSearch/ExaContents (neural + domain-scoped), direct curl of practice websites (contact / provider / about pages), the CMS NPI Registry API (npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api, version 2.1) for authorized-official name + title + owner designation, Community Impact Houston (best single source for dated 2025-2026 Houston clinic openings/relocations), EIN Presswire / AP press releases, Becker's ASC, Hospice News, InnovationMap, TMC.edu press releases, hitconsultant.net, Group Dentistry Now, and two live EA/practice-admin job postings. NO browser sessions were used. What was thin: (1) employee counts - almost no Houston private practice publishes headcount, so employee_count_estimate is null on most rows; where filled it comes from a LinkedIn company page workforce figure or a CMS-derived provider count and the source URL says which. (2) Named personal emails - practice sites publish info@/clinic@/kingwood@ style boxes almost exclusively, so contact_email is filled on exactly one row (Good Life Psychiatry's MD@ box, which is also recorded as company_email because it is a role address); 14 rows carry a company_email and the rest publish only a web form. (3) Dated trigger events - roughly two thirds of rows have a dated 2025-2026 trigger; the rest are honestly marked "other". A useful trick the verifier should know: for four rows (MAP Dental, Heights Behavioral Health, Good Life Psychiatry, North Houston Pulmonary) the NPI *enumeration_date* of the organization NPI is the practice-launch evidence, and that date is cited as trigger_date with the NPI record as trigger_source - it is a filing date, not a press announcement. Physician/owner titles were double-sourced by pairing the practice website bio against the NPI Registry authorized-official record (which carries an explicit title such as "Owner", "President", "Owner; Principal Shareholder"); where the NPI record was the only owner evidence I said so in notes. Three hiring_ea rows (DeliverIt Group, Vitalus Health, Rosarium Health) are the strongest in the set - all three are live postings for executive support to a founder/CEO, and Rosarium's is literally a "Chief of Staff to the CEO" req. Final counts: 28 candidates, 15 rejected, 26 with a published phone, 14 with a company_email, 1 with a named contact_email, 21 with a dated trigger. Deliberately excluded: Memorial Hermann, Houston Methodist, HCA, Baylor Medicine, CLS Health (200+ providers), Fondren Orthopedic, Advanced Orthopaedics & Sports Medicine, Choice Health at Home, New Day Healthcare, and Behavioral Innovations - all hospital-system-affiliated or clearly over 150 employees. Lena Health was moved to rejected because its own privacy policy gives an Austin legal address that conflicts with the Houston HQ on its LinkedIn page.
